newsitem.title: GREECE: US, UK firms to explore/drill for oil in Greece.
newsitem.headline: US, UK firms to explore/drill for oil in Greece.

text.p: Greece has picked Union Texas Transnational, U.S.-based Triton International Petroleum and Britain's Enterprise Oil Plc to explore and drill for oil in western Greece following an international tender.

A joint venture formed by Enterprise Oil and Union Texas Transnational with Enterprise Oil being the operator will carry out oil exploration and drilling in northwestern Peloponnese and Epirus, a development ministry statement said.
Triton International Petroleum was awarded the western Patras gulf area and the Aitolo-Akarnania region.
State Public Petroleum Corp (DEP) will participate with a 12 percent stake in the joint ventures for all four regions as per the tender.
"The companies will carry out extensive exploration programmes for the next 6-7 years with initial investments above $100 million," the ministry said.
It said that if two medium-size natural oil reserves are discovered total investment could reach $1 billion.
"This would cover about 20 percent of Greece's needs in petroleum and state revenues from leasing fees and taxes could reach $1.5 billion," it said.
Among the criteria used to select the companies emphasis was placed on their track record when drilling for oil in environmentally sensitive areas.
Enterprise Oil had 1995 assets of $3.3 billion and and average daily output of 235,000 barrels. It is active in Denmark, Norway, Italy and Britain.
Triton with assets of $825 million and average daily output of 20,000 barrels is active in China, Guatemala, Thailand and Malaysia.
Union Texas had 1995 assets of $1.8 billion and an output of 120,000 barrels.
